summary: Order submit failures (~31% error rate, 504 Gateway Timeout) originate from the external exchange partner, not from order-service v2.15.2. Fault onset is 11:01-11:02Z, coinciding with exchange-gateway logging connect timeouts to api.exchange-partner.example and 503 Service Unavailable responses from exchange-api. exchange-gateway's upstream latency rose from ~120ms to ~9300ms and upstream error rate from ~0.3% to ~45%, while exchange-gateway itself and order-service show no local resource anomaly (CPU/memory/pool/request-rate flat, no restarts). The reported order-service deploy at 10:48 was rolled back at 11:16 but the error rate never recovered (~31% through 12:45), ruling it out as the cause. ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner (exchange-api) outage causes exchange-gateway timeouts and order submit failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external provider api.exchange-partner.example began failing/timing out at ~11:01Z (connect timeouts after 5000ms and 503 Service Unavailable responses). exchange-gateway, which has no local resource issue, surfaces 504s to order-service, whose placeOrder path fails ~30%. The order-service release is coincidental and its rollback had no effect because the fault is external.

causal_chain.claim: order-service placeOrder to exchange-gateway returns 504 Gateway Timeout
Rollback of order-service v2.15.2 did not restore service, confirming the fault is not in order-service

assumptions: exchange-api has no telemetry in our stack, so its outage is inferred from exchange-gateway's upstream metrics and partner error bodies
the 503s with x-partner-request-id genuinely originate at the partner rather than a shared network egress layer

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 release introduced the failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The idempotency-key/retry-safe submit change in v2.15.2 caused order submit failures and the rollback should have recovered the service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rollback at 11:16 did not recover (error rate stayed ~31% through 12:45: F3); error onset at 11:02 postdates the 10:48 deploy by ~14 min and coincides with partner-side failures starting 11:01 (F5); all errors are exchange-gateway 504s, not order-service internal errors (F4); order-service CPU/pool/request-rate are normal (F9).

ranked_hypotheses.title: exchange-gateway local resource exhaustion or process failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: exchange-gateway ran out of CPU/memory or crashed, causing timeouts to order-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: exchange-gateway CPU ~30%, memory ~44%, 0 restarts, request_rate flat ~270 r/s (F8); the only degradation is on its upstream to the external provider (F7).

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine cache TTL config change degraded order flow
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 change at 09:20 caused downstream failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: pricing-engine error rate stayed flat ~0.2% (F11), change occurred 100+ min before onset, and no order-service error references pricing-engine (F4).

assumptions: exchange-api external provider has no telemetry in our stack; its fault is inferred from exchange-gateway upstream metrics and partner error payloads
the observed 503/x-partner-request-id responses genuinely originate at the partner and not at a shared egress/network layer
metric buckets are 900s aligned, so 1-2 min onset precision is limited

timeline.event: exchange-gateway first upstream connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example
exchange-api returns 503 Service Unavailable with x-partner-request-id
order-service first 504 Gateway Timeout on placeOrder
exchange-gateway circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47)
order-service v2.15.2 rolled back - error rate does not recover
Last exchange-gateway 504 error logged on order-service

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating this as order-service and engage the exchange partner / check partner status page; open a vendor incident for exchange-api.
recommended_actions.rationale: Partner returns 503 with x-partner-request-id and connect timeouts; fault is external.

recommended_actions.action: Fail over to a secondary exchange route or degrade gracefully (queue retries) instead of returning 504 on order submit.
recommended_actions.rationale: No secondary route exists in the dependency graph; HIST-103 resolution used exactly this.

recommended_actions.action: Verify post-rollback state and confirm keeping v2.15.2 is safe; the rollback was based on a false correlation.
recommended_actions.rationale: Rollback produced no recovery; re-deploying or re-investigating costs availability.

recommended_actions.action: Add telemetry/health checks for the external exchange-api and alert on exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate.
recommended_actions.rationale: exchange-api has_telemetry=false and the upstream degradation was only visible via exchange-gateway.

recommended_actions.action: Tune exchange-gateway circuit breaker/timeouts so order-service fails fast rather than piling up 5s waits.
recommended_actions.rationale: Client p99 rose to ~5s while 5000ms connect timeouts were hit repeatedly.

data_gaps: No direct telemetry from exchange-api (external, has_telemetry=false), so the partner-side root condition cannot be confirmed from our data - only inferred from exchange-gateway's upstream metrics and error bodies.

No packet-level/DNS/TLS egress data to fully rule out a shared network path fault between exchange-gateway and the partner; the single WARN 'deprecated TLS cipher offered by client' at 10:04:50Z is unexplained and not obviously causal.
order-service logs are truncated (349 matches, 40 returned); only the dominant 504 pattern was seen, so rarer error variants cannot be excluded.

findings.statement: order-service deployed v2.15.2 at 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z (change 'Add idempotency keys to order submit'); it was rolled back at 11:16:00Z.
order-service error rate was ~0.2% from 07:00 through the 10:45 bucket, then jumped to avg 26.73% at the 11:00 bucket and stayed ~31% (last 30.39%) through 12:45.
order-service error rate did NOT recover after the 11:16 rollback: it remains ~31% in every bucket from 11:15 through 12:45.
All 349 order-service ERROR entries share a single pattern: 'exchange-gateway call failed: <n> Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)', first seen 11:02:45Z, still occurring at 12:58:54Z.

exchange-gateway upstream connect timeouts and 503s begin at 11:01:25Z (upstream connect timeout host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder), about 13 minutes after the order-service deploy and about 2 minutes before order-service's first 504.

refs.quote: upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder

findings.statement: exchange-gateway logs show the external partner returning 503 Service Unavailable with x-partner-request-id values (161 occurrences) plus 163 placeOrder + 146 quoteSnapshot connect timeouts.

exchange-gateway's upstream to the partner degraded sharply: upstream_latency_ms went from ~120ms to ~8550ms at the 11:00 bucket, and upstream_error_rate from ~0.3% to ~42%, both sustained through 12:45.
exchange-gateway itself shows no local resource problem: CPU stayed ~30%, memory ~44%, restarts 0, and request_rate flat ~270 r/s across the whole window.
order-service local metrics are unchanged across the incident: CPU ~40%, db_pool_in_use ~14 connections, request_rate ~230 r/s.
order-service p99 latency jumped from ~150ms to ~4650-5300ms at the 11:00 bucket, consistent with waiting on the exchange-gateway timeout.

pricing-engine error rate stayed flat at ~0.2% throughout, and it has no shared dependency with order-service other than being a sibling; the only config change (pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 at 09:20) produced no measurable effect.
order-service has one dependency to exchange-gateway (http) and exchange-gateway calls exchange-api (external, has_telemetry=false); no alternate/secondary exchange route is present in the graph.
exchange-gateway had no code deployments in the 06:00-12:59 window.
